THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR HEARING THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of M.V.Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short)
challenging the judgment and award passed by MACT (SCCH-17) in M.V.C.No.7618/2010 dated 29.09.2012.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the parties herein are referred with original ranks occupied by them before the tribunal.

The brief factual matrix leading to the case are that on 25.09.2010 at 9.45 p.m. in front of MVIT main gate, Rajakunte Road when the deceased was riding the bicycle, the driver of the water tanker bearing registration No.KA-01-AB-4040 drove the same in a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the bicycle.
Due to the impact, deceased sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
The deceased was aged about 28 years and was working as a cook in MVIT Ladies Hostel, Bangalore and was earning Rs.4,500/- per month.

sentences.text: 4. The claimants are the dependants of the deceased and they lost the bread earner of the family.
Hence, they filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Act claiming compensation of Rs.10 Lakhs from the respondents.
5. The respondent No.1 has admitted the coverage of the policy of the vehicle bearing registration No. KA-01- AB-4040 but disputed the other assertions made in the claim petition.
It is contended that the vehicle was planted NC: 2023:KHC:40972 and there was no rash and negligent manner driving on the part of the driver of the lorry.

The respondent No.2 who was the owner though disputed the claim contended that the vehicle was duly insured with respondent No.1 and whatever the compensation is to be awarded needs to be indemnified by the respondent No.1.

6. The tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence has allowed the petition in part by awarding total compensation of Rs.5,94,000/- with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till its realization by fastening the liability on both the respondents.
Being aggrieved by this award, the respondent No.1-insurance company has filed this appeal.
7. Heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the appellant/insurance company and learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.
Perused the records.

The learned counsel for the appellant would contend that the involvement of the lorry in the accident itself is not established and the tribunal has not properly appreciated the facts and evidence in its proper perspective.

It is further asserted that the tribunal has not appreciated the oral and documentary evidence and failed to consider the negligence on the part of the deceased and hence,
he would seek for allowing the appeal.
9.
Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondents / claimants would support the judgment and award passed by the tribunal.
10. Having heard the arguments and perusing the records, the tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.5,94,000/- with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition.

11. The main contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the lorry was not at all involved in the accident and the complaint was an after thought story and a false complaint came to be filed by colluding with police NC: 2023:KHC:40972 authorities and hospital authorities.
It is also the specific contention that the tanker bearing registration No.KA-01- AB-4040 was not involved in the accident.
However, to substantiate this contention, the respondents have not led any evidence.
12. Though a similar contention was taken by respondent No.2 who is the owner, he did not step into the witness box to substantiate the said contention.
Apart from that RW1 was examined who was the officer of the insurance company but he had no personal knowledge regarding the accident.
Even the driver of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove that the vehicle was not involved in the accident.

sentences.text: Further, Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P1 is the FIR and Ex.P3 is the post mortem report, which disclose that the death is due to accidental injuries.

Ex.P8 is the charge sheet, which clearly discloses that the driver of the offending vehicle was prosecuted for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304A of Indian Penal NC: 2023:KHC:40972 Code, 1860.

These documents were not challenged by the owner-respondent No.2 and he has not made any attempts to examine the driver to prove the fact that his lorry was not involved in the accident.
14.
No doubt, there is some delay in lodging the complaint but mere delay in lodging the complaint cannot be considered so as to draw an inference that the lorry was planted subsequently.
There is a delay of one day in lodging the complaint and it is quite natural as the deceased was admitted in the hospital and claimants were under shock.
Under such circumstances, the delay itself cannot be a ground for discarding the evidence on record.
The respondents have not led any evidence to dislodge the presumptive value of documentary evidence produced by the claimants in the form of Ex.P1 to Ex.P8.

These documents prima facie establish that the offending lorry was involved in the accident and though certain allegations were made by respondent No.2 against the Investigating Officer by addressing a letter to the Commissioner, the NC: 2023:KHC:40972 same was not substantiated as respondent No.2 did not step into the witness box.
15. Considering these facts and circumstances, the contention that the lorry was not at all involved in the accident cannot be accepted.

The tribunal after appreciating the oral and documentary evidence has rightly held that the accident has occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending lorry and the said finding is based on proper appreciation of the evidence.
Hence, the said finding cannot be disturbed.

16. Further, the tribunal has considered the income of the deceased at Rs.4,000/- per month and by applying the multiplier of '17' and after deducting 1/3rd towards personal expenses, has awarded compensation of Rs.5,44,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.
The accident has occurred in the year 2010.
The tribunal has taken the notional income at Rs.4,000 per month which cannot be said to be on higher side and it is reasonable.
NC: 2023:KHC:40972 Hence, the compensation awarded by the tribunal cannot be said to exorbitant or excessive so as to call for any interference.
In fact, the compensation awarded under other heads is on the lower side and since, claimants are satisfied with the said compensation, it does not call for any interference.
17. Looking to these facts and circumstances, the appeal being devoid of any merits, the same does not survive for any consideration and accordingly, it is requires to be dismissed.
Hence, the appeal stands dismissed.
